author: DTrim99
body:
It isn't another credit — it's the rebate itself. PolicyEngine modeled the 2021 rebate as a **per-person** non-refundable credit ($1,250 in each spouse's column), and two things went wrong on your combined-separate return:

1. **Per-column clipping.** Your Form 2 columns are $4,195 (primary) and $506 (spouse), so the return's 2021 liability is $4,701 — well above $2,500, so the rebate should be the full $2,500. But the spouse's $506 column can't absorb their $1,250 half.
2. **Election flip.** Because the rebate was a non-refundable credit, it entered the separate-vs-joint election. With the rebate present PE elected *joint* (to use the full $2,500); when the emulator zeroes the rebate to measure `srebate`, PE re-elected *separate* (the cheaper base, $4,701). So `srebate` came out as $4,701 − $2,752 = **$1,949** instead of $2,500.

PE's underlying `mt_income_tax_rebate` was already $2,500; the shortfall was this modeling artifact. Fix is up ([PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9529](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/pull/9529), issue #9528): the rebate is now applied **once per return**, capped at the combined 2021 liability, and kept out of the filing election. On your record the emulator now returns **srebate $2,500** and siitax $2,201.39, and `staxbc` corrects to $4,701 (separate filing, matching your Form 2 columns). I'll ping you when it merges so you can rerun.
